metadata.title: A Short Introduction to Boosting
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json registry lists this as 'Adaptive Game Playing Using Multiplicative Weights' (Freund & Schapire). The PDF actually contains 'A Short Introduction to Boosting' (Freund & Schapire, J. Japanese Society for AI, 14(5):771-780, 1999). Extraction reflects the PDF contents.

nodes.name: PAC learning model
nodes.statement: Probably Approximately Correct learning model of Valiant: a framework for studying machine learning where an algorithm must, with high probability, output a hypothesis with small error.

nodes.name: Weak learning algorithm
nodes.statement: A learning algorithm that performs just slightly better than random guessing in the PAC model, i.e., produces a hypothesis $h_t$ whose error $\epsilon_t$ on distribution $D_t$ satisfies $\epsilon_t \le 1/2 - \gamma$ for some $\gamma > 0$.

nodes.name: Strong learning algorithm
nodes.statement: A learning algorithm that can generate a hypothesis with arbitrarily low error rate, given sufficient data.

nodes.name: Weak hypothesis error
nodes.statement: For weak hypothesis $h_t : X \to \{-1, +1\}$ trained on distribution $D_t$, the error is $\epsilon_t = \Pr_{i \sim D_t}[h_t(x_i) \ne y_i] = \sum_{i : h_t(x_i) \ne y_i} D_t(i)$.

nodes.name: Distribution update / weight $D_t(i)$
nodes.statement: $D_t(i)$ is the weight on training example $i$ at round $t$; $D_1(i) = 1/m$ initially and increases for misclassified examples so the weak learner focuses on hard examples.

nodes.name: Margin of an example
nodes.statement: For example $(x,y)$, the margin is $\mathrm{margin}(x,y) = \frac{y \sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x)}{\sum_t \alpha_t} \in [-1,+1]$; positive iff $H$ classifies $(x,y)$ correctly, with magnitude interpreted as confidence.

nodes.name: Instance vector and weight vector
nodes.statement: Instance vector $h(x) = \langle h_1(x), h_2(x), \dots, h_N(x) \rangle$ collects weak-hypothesis predictions on $x$; weight vector $\alpha = \langle \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \dots, \alpha_N \rangle$ collects the combination coefficients.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ and $\ell_\infty$ norms used by AdaBoost
nodes.statement: AdaBoost uses $\|\alpha\|_1 = \sum_t |\alpha_t|$ for the weight vector and $\|h(x)\|_\infty = \max_t |h_t(x)|$ for the instance vector.

nodes.name: VC-dimension
nodes.statement: A standard measure of the complexity of a hypothesis space, denoted $d$ for the weak hypothesis space.

nodes.name: AdaBoost
nodes.statement: Adaptive boosting algorithm of Freund and Schapire that maintains a distribution over training examples, repeatedly trains a weak learner, and outputs a weighted majority vote of the weak hypotheses.
input: Training set $(x_1, y_1), \dots, (x_m, y_m)$ with $x_i \in X$, $y_i \in Y = \{-1, +1\}$
nodes.notes: PDF math is degraded in places; pseudocode reconstructed from Figure 1.

nodes.name: Initialize distribution
nodes.statement: Set $D_1(i) = 1/m$ for all $i = 1, \dots, m$.

nodes.name: Main loop over rounds $t = 1, \dots, T$
nodes.statement: For $t = 1, \dots, T$: train weak learner on $D_t$ to obtain $h_t : X \to \{-1,+1\}$ with error $\epsilon_t = \Pr_{i \sim D_t}[h_t(x_i) \ne y_i]$; choose $\alpha_t = \tfrac{1}{2} \ln\!\left(\tfrac{1-\epsilon_t}{\epsilon_t}\right)$; update $D_{t+1}(i) = \frac{D_t(i) \exp(-\alpha_t y_i h_t(x_i))}{Z_t}$ where $Z_t$ normalizes $D_{t+1}$.

nodes.name: Output final hypothesis
nodes.statement: Return $H(x) = \mathrm{sign}\!\left( \sum_{t=1}^{T} \alpha_t h_t(x) \right)$.

nodes.name: AdaBoost.M1
nodes.statement: Most straightforward multiclass extension of AdaBoost; works when the weak learner can achieve reasonably high accuracy (better than 50%) on the hard distributions created by AdaBoost.

nodes.name: AdaBoost.MH
nodes.statement: Multiclass extension of Schapire and Singer that reduces the multiclass problem to binary problems of the form: 'For example $x$, is the correct label $y$ or one of the other labels?'

nodes.name: AdaBoost.M2 / AdaBoost.MR
nodes.statement: Multiclass extension creating, for each example $x$ with correct label $y$ and each incorrect label $y'$, a binary problem of the form: 'For $x$, is the correct label $y$ or $y'$?' AdaBoost.M2 is a special case of AdaBoost.MR.
nodes.origin_citation: Freund and Schapire 1997; Schapire and Singer 1998

nodes.name: Output-codes boosting
nodes.statement: Multiclass boosting technique that incorporates Dietterich and Bakiri's error-correcting output codes; achieves bounds similar to AdaBoost.MH/M2 and works with any binary weak learner.

nodes.name: Gentle AdaBoost
nodes.statement: Variant of AdaBoost suggested by Friedman, Hastie and Tibshirani that places less emphasis on outliers.

nodes.name: BrownBoost
nodes.statement: Adaptive version of Freund's boost-by-majority algorithm that de-emphasizes outliers when they appear too hard to classify; reveals connections to Brownian motion.

nodes.name: Weak-hypothesis error
nodes.statement: $\epsilon_t = \Pr_{i \sim D_t}[h_t(x_i) \ne y_i] = \sum_{i : h_t(x_i) \ne y_i} D_t(i).$

nodes.name: Coefficient $\alpha_t$
nodes.statement: $\alpha_t = \tfrac{1}{2} \ln\!\left( \tfrac{1 - \epsilon_t}{\epsilon_t} \right).$

nodes.name: Multiplicative weight update
nodes.statement: $D_{t+1}(i) = \frac{D_t(i) \exp(-\alpha_t y_i h_t(x_i))}{Z_t}$ where $Z_t$ is a normalization factor.

nodes.name: Final hypothesis
nodes.statement: $H(x) = \mathrm{sign}\!\left( \sum_{t=1}^{T} \alpha_t h_t(x) \right).$

nodes.name: Training-error bound
nodes.statement: $\Pr[H(x) \ne y] \le \prod_t 2 \sqrt{\epsilon_t (1 - \epsilon_t)} = \prod_t \sqrt{1 - 4 \gamma_t^2} \le \exp\!\left( -2 \sum_t \gamma_t^2 \right),$ where $\epsilon_t = 1/2 - \gamma_t$.

nodes.name: Generalization-error bound (VC)
nodes.statement: $\widehat{\Pr}[H(x) \ne y] + \tilde{O}\!\left( \sqrt{\tfrac{T d}{m}} \right),$ where $T$ is the number of rounds, $d$ is the VC-dimension of the weak hypothesis space and $m$ is the sample size.

nodes.name: Margin
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{margin}(x,y) = \frac{y \sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x)}{\sum_t \alpha_t}.$

nodes.name: Margin-based generalization bound
nodes.statement: $\widehat{\Pr}[\mathrm{margin}(x,y) \le \theta] + \tilde{O}\!\left( \sqrt{\tfrac{d}{m \theta^2}} \right),$ for any $\theta > 0$ with high probability; this bound is independent of $T$.

nodes.name: Maximum-minimum-margin objective
nodes.statement: $\max_{\alpha} \min_{i} \frac{(\alpha \cdot h(x_i)) y_i}{\|\alpha\| \cdot \|h(x_i)\|}.$ For AdaBoost the norms are $\|\alpha\|_1$ and $\|h(x)\|_\infty$; for SVMs both norms are $\ell_2$.

nodes.name: Training-error bound for AdaBoost
nodes.statement: If each weak hypothesis has error $\epsilon_t = 1/2 - \gamma_t$, the training error of the final hypothesis $H$ satisfies $\Pr[H(x) \ne y] \le \prod_t \sqrt{1 - 4 \gamma_t^2} \le \exp(-2 \sum_t \gamma_t^2)$.
assumptions: Each weak hypothesis $h_t$ has error $\epsilon_t = 1/2 - \gamma_t$ on its training distribution $D_t$
conclusions: Training error of the final hypothesis $H$ is at most $\prod_t 2 \sqrt{\epsilon_t(1-\epsilon_t)} = \prod_t \sqrt{1 - 4 \gamma_t^2} \le \exp(-2 \sum_t \gamma_t^2)$
If $\gamma_t \ge \gamma > 0$ for all $t$, the training error drops exponentially fast in $T$

nodes.name: VC-style generalization bound for AdaBoost
nodes.statement: With high probability, the generalization error of the final hypothesis is at most $\widehat{\Pr}[H(x) \ne y] + \tilde{O}\!\left( \sqrt{T d / m} \right)$, where $d$ is the VC-dimension of the weak hypothesis space.
conclusions: Generalization error of $H$ is at most $\widehat{\Pr}[H(x) \ne y] + \tilde{O}\!\left( \sqrt{T d / m} \right)$
nodes.origin_citation: Freund and Schapire 1997 (using Baum and Haussler 1989)

nodes.name: Margin-based generalization bound
nodes.statement: For any $\theta > 0$, with high probability the generalization error of $H$ is at most $\widehat{\Pr}[\mathrm{margin}(x,y) \le \theta] + \tilde{O}\!\left( \sqrt{d / (m \theta^2)} \right)$. The bound is independent of the number of rounds $T$.
conclusions: Bound is independent of $T$, explaining the empirical absence of overfitting

nodes.name: Boosting concentrates on small-margin examples
nodes.statement: Boosting is particularly aggressive at increasing the margin (in a quantifiable sense) since it concentrates on the examples with the smallest margins (positive or negative).
conclusions: AdaBoost increases margins of training examples even after training error reaches zero
Continued margin growth corresponds to continued drop in test error

nodes.name: Hypothesis boosting problem
nodes.statement: Given a weak learning algorithm that performs slightly better than random guessing in the PAC model, can it be boosted into an arbitrarily accurate strong learning algorithm?

nodes.name: Horse-racing gambler
nodes.statement: A gambler extracts many rough rules of thumb from an expert by presenting different collections of races; combining these rules of thumb illustrates the boosting paradigm of turning weak rules into a strong predictor.

nodes.name: Boosting C4.5 on the letter dataset
nodes.statement: Empirical demonstration (Schapire et al. 1998) that boosting Quinlan's C4.5 on the UCI letter dataset continues to drive down test error long after training error reaches zero, with margin distributions shifting upward over rounds.

nodes.name: Boosting decision stumps and C4.5 on UCI benchmarks
nodes.statement: On 27 UCI benchmark datasets, boosting decision stumps performs comparably to C4.5 alone, while boosting C4.5 yields significant improvements (Freund and Schapire 1996).

nodes.name: Text categorization with AdaBoost
nodes.statement: Schapire and Singer applied AdaBoost (with weak hypotheses testing word/phrase presence) to Reuters newswire articles and AP newswire headlines, outperforming naive Bayes, probabilistic TF-IDF, Rocchio and sleeping experts on most measures.

nodes.name: OCR outlier identification
nodes.statement: Freund and Schapire showed on an OCR task that the highest-weight examples after several rounds of boosting are typically mislabeled or inherently ambiguous digits, illustrating AdaBoost's ability to identify outliers.

nodes.name: Adaptivity of AdaBoost
nodes.statement: Unlike previous boosting algorithms that required an a priori known lower bound $\gamma$ on the weak edge, AdaBoost adapts to the actual error rates of the individual weak hypotheses; the 'Ada' is short for 'adaptive'.

nodes.name: AdaBoost vs SVM: norms and computation
nodes.statement: AdaBoost and SVMs both seek a max-min margin classifier but differ in: (i) norms ($\ell_1/\ell_\infty$ vs $\ell_2/\ell_2$), (ii) optimization (linear vs quadratic programming), and (iii) high-dimensional search strategy (greedy via weak learner vs kernel trick).

nodes.name: Game-theoretic interpretation
nodes.statement: Boosting can be viewed as repeated play of a certain game; AdaBoost is a special case of a more general algorithm for playing repeated games and approximately solving a game, connecting boosting to linear programming and online learning.
nodes.origin_citation: Freund and Schapire 1996, 1999; Grove and Schuurmans 1998; Breiman 1997

nodes.name: Gradient-descent interpretation of boosting
nodes.statement: Schapire and Singer's generalization of AdaBoost interprets the algorithm as coordinate-wise gradient descent on a potential function over the space of linear classifiers in weak hypotheses.

nodes.name: Sensitivity to noise and outliers
nodes.statement: Boosting is especially susceptible to noise (Dietterich); when outliers are very numerous, the emphasis on hard examples can hurt performance, motivating Gentle AdaBoost and BrownBoost.
